title: Lattice–AMI WEF depth-3 named representatives and policy outputs
summary: Depth 3 identifies a historical CEO sponsor and a current Coherent executive participant, plus an SIA-to-WEF semiconductor-policy amplification path; no named Lattice WEF delegate is found.

data.question: Which named people represent the Lattice-adjacent Coherent and SIA networks inside WEF communities, and what concrete outputs or policy pathways are visible?
data.method: Primary-source person-resolution, community-roster review, publication tracing and bounded policy-link analysis.
data.framework: Named-representative and concrete-output mapping with explicit separation of membership, participation, authorship, advocacy and control.
data.scope: Coherent/II-VI WEF participation, current WEF initiative rosters, WEF workforce publications, SIA semiconductor policy advocacy and WEF policy coverage reviewed through 2026-07-27.
findings: Historical named sponsor: II-VI CEO Vincent D. Mattera Jr. publicly endorsed the company's 2021 partnership with WEF's Advanced Manufacturing & Production Platform.
Current named participant: WEF lists Coherent Chief People Officer Grace Lee as a member of the Frontline Talent Excellence Community.
The Frontline Talent initiative hosts quarterly executive exchanges and collaborative initiatives and has produced public workforce-transformation playbooks and white papers.
Coherent is also listed in WEF's C-level operations, supply-chain and procurement community, but the public organization record does not name its delegate.

SIA President and CEO John Neuffer publicly advocated for the Building Chips in America Act; WEF later published an explanatory article using SIA data and rationale while noting environmental criticism.
No reviewed public WEF roster, report or company disclosure names a current Lattice employee as Lattice's WEF centre representative.
conclusions: The Coherent path now contains both historical CEO-level sponsorship and current named executive participation, making it a stronger personnel link than the public Lattice profile alone.

The concrete WEF outputs found at this layer concern workforce transformation, human-machine collaboration and manufacturing/supply-chain strategy—not consumer ownership, firmware licensing or BIOS subscription policy.
The SIA path demonstrates semiconductor-policy advocacy followed by WEF editorial amplification; it does not establish joint authorship, joint lobbying or control of the Lattice–AMI transaction.

The next evidence-bearing layer is technical governance: standards bodies, firmware-resilience specifications, signing-key authority, anti-rollback rules, remote-management protocols and repairability constraints.
recommendations: Trace Lattice, AMI and named technical leaders through UEFI Forum, DMTF, Trusted Computing Group, Open Compute Project and NIST platform-firmware-resilience records.
Map Aptio, MegaRAC, Tektagon and Lattice Sentry update authority, signing-key custody, recovery policy, anti-rollback and third-party firmware compatibility.
Search for consumer-device licensing, repair restrictions, end-of-support rules and subscription-linked firmware capabilities separately from enterprise BMC products.
counterarguments: A company executive appearing on a WEF community roster does not prove the executive authored every community output.
WEF publication of an article citing SIA positions can be ordinary editorial coverage rather than coordinated advocacy.
The absence of a named Lattice representative in reviewed public records does not prove that no non-public representative exists.
limitations: Community pages do not disclose internal votes, attendance histories, fees or decision rights.
The reviewed Frontline Talent white-paper page does not attribute a specific recommendation to Grace Lee.
No public delegate was identified for Coherent's operations and supply-chain officers community record.
unresolved: Identity of Lattice's representative to the WEF advanced-manufacturing centre.
Identity of Coherent's delegate to the WEF operations and supply-chain officers community.
Any specific WEF report section, recommendation or vote attributable to Grace Lee or another named Coherent executive.
Technical standards and governance paths affecting firmware autonomy, repairability and update authority.

caveats: Institutional membership and community participation are not evidence of transaction command.
No consumer firmware-rental or kill-switch programme was established in this pass.

unresolved: specific individual authorship of WEF workforce outputs

workflow.next_action: Run firmware standards and governance depth-4 target.

title: Lattice–AMI firmware standards, update authority and repairability
summary: Depth-4 target tracing technical standards, named leaders and governance mechanisms that determine firmware signing, authenticated updates, anti-rollback, remote management and third-party repairability.

data.target: Lattice–AMI firmware standards, update authority and repairability governance
data.research_question: Which standards bodies, named technical leaders, specifications and vendor policies govern Lattice and AMI firmware authentication, signing keys, anti-rollback, recovery, remote management, interoperability and repairability?
hypotheses: Lattice and AMI participate in standards bodies that shape server and client firmware-management rules.
Authenticated update and recovery designs may centralize signing-key and rollback authority without necessarily requiring subscription licensing.
Enterprise BMC subscription models and consumer Aptio licensing must be distinguished.
objectives: Map UEFI Forum, DMTF, Trusted Computing Group, Open Compute Project and NIST platform-firmware-resilience connections.
Identify named Lattice and AMI representatives, contributors, board members and working-group participants.
Trace Aptio, MegaRAC, Tektagon and Lattice Sentry specifications and update-control architecture.
Determine signing-key custody, anti-rollback policy, recovery authority, third-party firmware support and end-of-support behavior.
Search for consumer-device licensing, repairability restrictions and subscription-linked firmware functions.
in_scope: vendor technical documentation and security advisories
NIST SP 800-193 and related platform-firmware-resilience guidance
UEFI, Redfish, PLDM, SPDM, TPM and platform-root-of-trust governance
consumer and enterprise licensing and support policies
selection_reason: Depth 3 found no WEF consumer-firmware policy output.
The material ownership and lock-in question depends on technical standards, key custody and licensing rather than institutional membership alone.
The Lattice–AMI combination joins programmable control hardware with foundational firmware and remote-management products.

caveats: Technical capability must not be converted into a claim of malicious intent without product or policy evidence.

workflow.next_action: Trace standards-body rosters, specifications, signing-key authority, licensing and repairability policies.

title: Lattice–AMI WEF named representatives depth-3 pass
summary: Completed person-level and output-level expansion identifying Vincent Mattera, Grace Lee and John Neuffer, while selecting firmware technical governance as the final depth.

data.research_question: Which named representatives and concrete policy or publication outputs connect the Lattice-adjacent Coherent and SIA networks to WEF?
data.method: Official company, WEF initiative, community-roster, publication and semiconductor-policy source reconciliation.
classification_rules: Roster membership is recorded separately from authorship or decision authority.
Company succession is qualified when mapping II-VI records to Coherent.
WEF editorial coverage is not normalized into joint lobbying or coauthorship.
Failure to find a public delegate is recorded as unresolved, not as proof of absence.

findings.finding: Vincent D. Mattera Jr. was the named CEO sponsor of II-VI's 2021 WEF advanced-manufacturing partnership.
Grace Lee of Coherent is a current named member of WEF's Frontline Talent Excellence Community.
Coherent has an organization record in WEF's C-level operations and supply-chain officers community, but its delegate is not public.
The Frontline Talent initiative has concrete workforce publications and structured executive exchanges.
John Neuffer advocated for the Building Chips Act, and WEF later summarized the policy while citing industry rationale and criticism.
No named current Lattice WEF delegate or consumer-firmware ownership policy was found in reviewed public records.

provenance.method: Public-source recursive OSINT with bounded inference

workflow.next_action: Run firmware standards and governance depth-4 target.
